title: R' Avdumi Malcha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman mentions him near the end of chapter 4 of Bava Metzia as a meat seller who used to soak lean meat in water. R’ Yaakov bar Acha said to him, “But have we not learned …?” Hyman also cites Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 2:5, where he slept outside the sukkah because he was guarding his shop. R’ Chiya bar Abba passed by and forbade him to do so.

notes.text: The first work abbreviation ב״ה, followed by “end of chapter 4,” has not been securely identified.

The saved whole Venice JerusalemTalmudBavaMetzia4:7 scalar, internally headed halakhah9, names abbreviated R' Avduma Malcha and Yaakov bar Acha’s אין מפרקסין challenge. This matches the first notice despite supplied ב״ה and the earlier אבדומי exact-spelling nonmatch, without proving a printed letter repair. Hyman’s meat-selling/lean-meat-soaking description remains his paraphrase; the named מפתר סרדוותיה was not independently interpreted here. Sukkah2:5 remains an inherited search lead, not a newly fetched primary paragraph. ואסרו contextually prohibits sleeping outside the sukkah. No uninspected full Rabbi titles are inferred.

Hyman’s printed edition reads ב״מ, Bava Metzia, where the supplied transcription has ב״ה. The print and indexed Hebrew title call him Avdumi Malcha with a ḥet (מלחא). The parallel in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 4:7 names Avduma Malcha and records Yaakov bar Acha’s objection about making goods look better. Guggenheimer renders the name Eudaimon the salt dealer and gives several interpretations of the activity. The meat interpretation he reports is close to Hyman’s. Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 2:5 likewise has Avduma Malcha sleeping in front of his shop and Chiya telling him to sleep in his sukkah. Its Hebrew has Chiya bar Ba, rendered bar Abba by Guggenheimer. Hyman describes guarding the shop.
